title: Global refinement of modifications over a finite open cover
statement: Let $S$ be integral Noetherian and $S=\bigcup_{i=1}^n U_i$ a finite open cover. For each $i$ let $q_i:V_i\to U_i$ be a modification [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Then there exists a modification $q:S'\to S$ such that, for every $i$, the restriction $S'\times_S U_i\to U_i$ factors through $q_i$. In particular, finitely many modifications of $S$ have a common modification refinement. All the factorization morphisms are over the indicated base.

source.place: §2.1, p. 3, affine-local reduction and globalization of modifications; the finite-cover argument used there. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Every open subset of $S$ is quasi-compact: given an open covering of an open $O$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to the nonempty family of complements in $S$ of finite unions of members of that covering. A minimal complement cannot decrease when one more member is added, so its complementary finite union contains every covering member and equals $O$. The same conclusion holds for every open subscheme of $S$. For such a subscheme $T$, inverse images of affine opens under its diagonal are open subsets of $T$, hence quasi-compact. Thus $T$ is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and is qcqs by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. In particular this applies to $S$ and every $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology; elementary minimal-complement argument and the definition of quasi-separatedness

proof.text: Discard the indices with $U_i=\varnothing$ for the construction; their required factorizations are the unique maps from the empty scheme. For each remaining $i$, choose an open $D_i\subset U_i$ over which $q_i$ is an isomorphism, as supplied by [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Each $D_i$ is nonempty and open in $S$. The scheme $S$ is nonempty and irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]; therefore the finite intersection $W=\bigcap_iD_i$ is nonempty, open, dense in $S$ and dense in every nonempty $U_i$. It is quasi-compact by step 1, lies in every such $U_i$, and $q_i^{-1}(W)\to W$ is an isomorphism. The intersection is nonempty because otherwise the finitely many proper closed complements would cover an irreducible space.

source.place: Tag 081T, lemma-dominate-modification-by-blowup, choice of the preserved quasi-compact isomorphism open; finite intersection argument

proof.text: Fix a remaining $i$. Properness of $q_i$ includes separatedness and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The qcqs and quasi-compactness conditions for $(T,U,q)=(U_i,W,q_i)$ were proved in steps 1--2. Apply [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-elimination] to choose a $W$-admissible blow-up $b_i:B_i\to U_i$ whose strict transform $p_i:Z_i\to B_i$ of $V_i$ is an open immersion. Choose it with $b_i^{-1}(W)$ schematically dense in $B_i$, as that statement permits. Admissibility means the finite-type center ideal is the unit ideal on $W$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup].

The strict transform $Z_i$ is a closed subscheme of $V_i\times_{U_i}B_i$ containing its part over the complement of the blow-up center [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Since that complement contains $W$, its image under $p_i$ contains $b_i^{-1}(W)$. The projection $V_i\times_{U_i}B_i\to B_i$ is a closed map by the universally closed clause of properness in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the image of its closed subset $Z_i$ is closed. By step 3 this image contains a dense subset of $B_i$, so it is all of $B_i$. A surjective open immersion identifies its source with the entire target open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]; hence $p_i$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse followed by the projection to $V_i$ gives a morphism $h_i:B_i\to V_i$ with $q_i h_i=b_i$. This is a morphism over $U_i$, since both strict-transform projections come from the same fibre product.

source.place: Tag 081T, lemma-dominate-modification-by-blowup, expanded final argument (the source says some details omitted)

proof.text: The open $W$ is contained in $U_i$, and $S,U_i,W$ satisfy all quasi-compactness hypotheses. The extension assertion of [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-blowups], with $(T,U,V)=(S,W,U_i)$, extends $b_i$ to a $W$-admissible blow-up $a_i:A_i\to S$ whose base change to $U_i$ is $b_i:B_i\to U_i$. Do this for every remaining index. The first assertion of the same node then supplies a common $W$-admissible blow-up $q:S'\to S$ and morphisms $r_i:S'\to A_i$ over $S$. Only finitely many extensions are needed. No identification of the different local modifications on overlaps is required for this construction.

Base change $r_i$ to $U_i$. Under the extension identification in step 5, this gives $S'\times_SU_i\to A_i\times_SU_i\simeq B_i$. Compose it with $h_i:B_i\to V_i$ from step 4. The equation $q_i h_i=b_i$ and the fact that $r_i$ is over $S$ show that the composite followed by $q_i$ is exactly $S'\times_SU_i\to U_i$. These maps are the maps of fibre products determined by their two projections [def-pc-fibre-product], so every asserted factorization is over $U_i$. For a discarded empty $U_i$, the same assertion holds by the unique empty-source morphism.

source.place: Tags 080M and 080N, restriction and composition of the resulting factorization morphisms

proof.text: The map $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper]. It is an isomorphism over $W$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open]. The inverse image of $W$ is topologically dense in $S'$ by [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup], applied to the dense quasi-compact open $W\subset S$ and the $W$-admissible blow-up $q$. These are precisely the modification conditions of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. For finitely many modifications of $S$, use the finite cover with every $U_i=S$ and apply the construction just proved. For the empty family take the identity of $S$: its diagonal is a closed immersion, its affine coordinate maps are generated by the empty set, and all its base changes are identity closed maps, so it is proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and is a modification with preserved open $S$.

source.place: Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor (complement and exceptional divisor); Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective (properness); the existing admissible blow-up density lemma and modification definition

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q66-d3c28a032 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the parent lem-trf-orgogozo-good-modification and every cited statement, including the blueprint_update versions. Checked the Stacks sources locally: flat.tex Tags 081S and 081T (081T's proof ends 'some details omitted') and divisors.tex Tags 080M and 080N. The Orgogozo paper and RG71 I §5.3.3 are not in literature/; the report correctly lists them as WANTED and marks the proof as agent-written. The statement is not weakened, and the parent's three uses need exactly it. Step 1: the minimal-closed-subset argument shows every open of S is quasi-compact, and quasi-separatedness follows from the definition. Step 2: W, the intersection of the opens D_i where each q_i is an isomorphism, is nonempty, dense and quasi-compact because S is irreducible. Step 3: the elimination statement applies to (U_i, W, q_i) and all its hypotheses hold. If its density clause is read narrowly, the already-cited lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup still gives topological density, which is all step 4 needs. Step 4 correctly writes out the omitted details of 081T: the strict transform is closed and the projection is a closed map, so the image is closed and contains a dense set; the open immersion is therefore surjective, hence an isomorphism, and gives h_i with q_i h_i = b_i. Step 5 applies the extension (080M) and common blow-up (080N) clauses with W inside U_i. Steps 6 and 7 follow from the fibre-product universal property and from properness, the isomorphism over W and density for the blow-up q, which are exactly the modification conditions. The finite-family and empty-family cases are correct. Edge cases tested: a field base, n=1, repeated opens, an empty U_i, a nonreduced V_i, and a non-separated S. There are no new nodes. A DAG grep for 081S/081T/081U/080M/080N, dominate and common modification found no duplicate. All cited off-unit statements are closed in slopmaster2, so they count as tools and the route is fine. Accepted the three declared tool_uses: the Noetherian minimal closed subset lemma, sk-lem-nagata-sketch-elimination and sk-lem-nagata-sketch-blowups. No SGA source is used, and no changes were made.

lean.statement: theorem exists_modification_zariski_refinement (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → S.Opens) (hcover : (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤) (V : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (q : ∀ i : Fin n, V i ⟶ (U i).toScheme) (hq : ∀ i : Fin n, @IsModification (V i) (U i).toScheme inferInstance inferInstance (isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp (TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.isCompact (U i : Set S))) (q i)) : ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (p : S' ⟶ S), IsModification p ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ a : pullback p (U i).ι ⟶ V i, a ≫ q i = pullback.snd p (U i).ι
